questions.q: What mistake does this lesson warn against making before scoping the problem?
options: Jumping straight to CREATE INDEX or rewriting a query before investigating
Writing down a five-step plan before touching SSMS
Asking whether the problem is new or ongoing
Checking what's actually running first
questions.explain: Guessing at a fix — usually adding an index — before scoping the problem is how real troubleshooting time gets wasted.

questions.q: What do both departments' complaints suggest about whether this is new or ongoing?
options: Both said the problem began yesterday after a deployment
Both said the problem only happens once a month
Only Billing reported an ongoing pattern
Neither said 'this just started' — both describe an ongoing, every-morning pattern
questions.explain: Both departments describe a recurring, every-morning pattern, not a sudden one-time regression.

questions.q: What is the correct order of this chapter's five-step investigation plan?
options: Identify active sessions, find slow queries, read the plan, diagnose, fix and re-test
Read the plan first, then decide whether to look at sessions at all
Diagnose, fix, identify sessions, find slow queries, read the plan
Fix and re-test, then figure out what was wrong afterward
questions.explain: Each step produces evidence the next step depends on: sessions, then slow queries, then the plan, then diagnosis, then the fix.

questions.q: Why isn't 'just add an index everywhere it might help' actually a faster plan?
options: Indexes aren't free — they slow down writes — and this investigation turns up more than one real cause
There is only one cause in this scenario, so an index fixes everything
Indexes have no cost at all, so this reasoning doesn't apply here
Azure SQL Database doesn't allow creating new indexes
questions.explain: Every index adds write overhead, and this investigation turns up more than one real root cause — a blanket indexing approach would miss the second one.

questions.q: What should be ready before starting Lesson 3?
options: A rollback plan for the Beginner project's backups
A finished CREATE INDEX script
SSMS or Azure Data Studio connected to OverlookClinicalDB, ready to query
A completed execution plan for every query in the database
questions.explain: Lesson 3 starts Step 1 — querying active sessions — which requires an active connection to OverlookClinicalDB.
